mod.name: DAHM/DorHUD Framework + mod collection
mod.desc:
NOTE: Due to many requests I decided to post this here. Since I'd rather have everything in one place and there's too much info for a comments section, I made a Steam group for the mod.

The mod, called DAHM (formerly known as DorHUD, but use whatever you like), is basically a collection of modifications to (in my eyes) improve the game. The core is comparable to BLT, but has a bunch of extra features and is now (almost) fully compatible with BLT since version 1.6. The mod is a framework that provides a way to add sub-modules, so that the whole thing is very customizable. The basic version comes bundled with a bunch of default submods to provide the most requested features without being intrusive or gameplay altering (for the most part).

The game is no longer officially supported and I therefore I assume that the executable will not be updated. If this is the case, then the mod has to be updated. But for now it fixes a few bugs, some well known and other not so much. I tried to patch the game crashing bugs, but I'm pretty sure I didn't get them all. A more known bug is that the Vyse masks (and others) disappear from time to time. This is because the Steam community group page is fetched and then checked for the presence of your Steam ID. This is not very reliable, so I replaced it with a call to your local Steam client to the groups you're in. Another thing is that the mute state is now preserved between games, so you don't have to mute people on every single map. And you can open the menu when someone is loading, etc., etc., etc. Just don't expect all solutions to be very elegant ;).

The majority of the sub-modules involve anticheat stuff and profile checking, simply because there are so many cheaters in this game that think they can do that without any consequences. Those that still want to ruin my games can only do it once with that account before they (manually) get added to a banlist. For now the list is only local, so nothing is shared (unless you count the manual sharing of it). Furthermore, there is a very simplistic HUD addon to keep track of the game time and the kills you've made, there's a new difficulty, you can add your own matchmaking filters and there's the possibility to ban players both by keeping a local file and by blocking them on Steam (the latter requires the provided hook).

Since I don't want to type things twice, more specific information can be found on the Steam group page. That's also where I try to provide support and where updates will be posted, so that everything is kept in one place.

*Not all mods are posted to this website. Some smaller mods are posted in the [DAHM Downloads forum](https://steamcommunity.com/groups/dahm4pd/discussions/3/).*

mod.name: mod_overrides and DB:create_entry for PAYDAY: The Heist
mod.desc:
# **This mod is deprecated with the release of [Update 23 for PAYDAY: The Heist](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/24240/view/689771494788563593). This page is kept up only for historical reference and use with older versions of the game**

Ports `mod_overrides`, `DB:create_entry`, `DB:remove_entry` and `DB:reload_override_mods` from PAYDAY 2 and RAID to PAYDAY: The Heist.

## How does it work?
It works exactly the same as it does for PAYDAY 2: create a folder inside of the `assets` folder called `mod_overrides`.

## Does this depend on any other mods?
No, it does not require any other mods to work.

## Installation Guide
Download the zip folder, and unpack `DINPUT8.dll` and `PDTHModOverrides.dll` to your install folder.
For those playing on Linux: add `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="DINPUT8=n,b" %command%` to your launch options.
To Uninstall: Delete `DINPUT8.dll` and `PDTHModOverrides.dll`.
### Updating from the previous release
Those who are updating from the previous release (uses `VERSION.dll`), delete `VERSION.dll` and update as normal.

## How can I port my PDMod mods to this?
Rename the `.pdmod` file to `.zip` and extract its contents into its own mod_overrides folder with the password `0$45'5))66S2ixF51a<6}L2UK`.

**Or**: use [.pdmod Extractor](https://modworkshop.net/mod/53516)

## What files can I override with this?
All file types can be overriden.
`.dds` and `.bik` files will be interpreted as `.texture` and `.movie` respectively.

## Can this add any new files to the game?
Yes! With version 2.0 `DB:create_entry` has been backported and is available via Lua. This is not bound to any mod loader, anything that can execute Lua in-game can access these functions.
### Backported Lua Functions
 - `DB:create_entry(type, name, filepath)` filepath must be relative to the game's install folder, not your mod folder. type and name accept Idstrings and normal strings. Overwriting existing game files is supported. Example: `DB:create_entry("unit", "units/myunit/myunit", "./mods/mymod/myunit.unit")`
   Custom packages can be added by just setting the type in `create_entry` to `package` and providing it a valid package file.
 - `DB:remove_entry(type, name)` type and name accept Idstrings and normal strings. Removing a file critical to the game and not replacing it will crash the game. Example: `DB:remove_entry("unit", "units/characters/bain/bain")`
 - `DB:reload_override_mods()` (will reload the `mod_overrides` folder)

#### Source Code
Source Code: https://github.com/HW12Dev/PDTHModOverrides

mod.name: _hud - _atom's atrocious hud mod for PAYDAY: The Heist
mod.desc:
This is a customizable HUD mod for PAYDAY: The Heist with mostly aesthetic/quality of life changes.

# Features
* [Dropdown menus](https://modworkshop.net/mod/43115) for your loadout items for quick selection.
* A [custom interface](https://modworkshop.net/mod/51818) to quickly change your mask set and character.
* An option to color code deployable and player contours. (deployable contour colors require the peer_equipment module to be enabled)
* The ability to see the remaining charges of deployables in form of a text in the 3d environment. (requires the peer_equipment module to be enabled)
* A custom player label panel which adds a health bar on top of your teammate's heads.
* A custom player health interface with interchangeable designs to match your teammate mugshot panels or look like RAIDs player health interface.
* A custom weapon panel design and the option to show magazine ammo on top of your unequiped weapon icons in the vanilla panel.
* A custom drop-in panel which supports the display of multiple players joining at once and has the option to show each player's equipped loadout plus the ability to see their installed gameplay changing mods.
* A ported version of PAYDAY 2's assault and point of no return panels.
* An option to show reload and shotgun fire timers on screen.

# Notes
* This mod uses DAHMs hud module as a dependency, in order to use this hud you must have said module enabled.
* Deployable contours will not apply for some deployables if you drop-in after they were already placed and the host is not running DAHM.
* There may be some incompatibilities with WTFBM, I do not plan to develop compatibility with said hud.

# Credits:
* DorentuZ` - Assistance with development and the inclusion of specific changes in the framework so I could expand my mod.
* @neonsynth - Testing, German localization.
* Sergeant Panda - Testing since early versions of the mod and making me go insane by finding the most nefarious bugs known to mankind.
* @kfcdragon756 - Chinese localization.

[Source Code](https://github.com/mbien1981/_hud)

Those that still want to ruin my games can only do it once with that account before they (manually) get added to a banlist. For now the list is only local, so nothing is shared (unless you count the manual sharing of it). Furthermore, there is a very simplistic HUD addon to keep track of the game time and the kills you've made, there's a new difficulty, you can add your own matchmaking filters and there's the possibility to ban players both by keeping a local file and by blocking them on Steam (the latter requires the provided hook).

Since I don't want to type things twice, more specific information can be found on the Steam group page. That's also where I try to provide support and where updates will be posted, so that everything is kept in one place.

*Not all mods are posted to this website. Some smaller mods are posted in the [DAHM Downloads forum](https://steamcommunity.com/groups/dahm4pd/discussions/3/).*

detail.name: F.U.B.A.R. (Difficulty Enhancer)
detail.desc:
This is a project I've been working on for quite a good while, good month or two I think? I never really keep up with time these days. Anyhow this will up the difficulty by a lot, especially on Overkill and above. This does that by allowing certain enemies to have additional weapons that they don't normally have, upping the number of specials that spawn as well as the cap on specials, raising the number of cops that can be present, replacing enemies, adding new custom events, adding events and changes from Overkill 145+ onto the lower difficulties such as bulldozers being present in the vault on First World Bank, and having bonus mutators that turns this game into a nightmare for even the most seasoned players.

Here's the trailers for this in case you want some videos to see what you're in for:

Trailer 2: https://youtu.be/2IQgn28sCT8

detail.instructions:
To install: 
Step 1: Place folders mutator_fubar+_release, mutator_fubar_bonus_release, and mutator_fubar_release into the mods folder.
Step 2: Download Warmod
Step 3: Unzip and find a folder labeled scripts
Step 4: Find files named missionscriptcontroller and missionscriptcontroller2
Step 5: Delete these files
Step 6: Go into folder labeled fubar_additions_release and copy its contents
Step 7: Find folder within the Warmod folder labeled configs
Step 8: Open this folder and paste what you copied in step 6.
Step 9: Copy Warmod folder into mods

If anyone has problems doing this feel free to leave a comment and I will help you when I can.

mod.name: Warmod 1.2.0
mod.desc:
This mod provides you some features to make your gameplay much more challenging. Because the vanilla game is so easy and boring, right?
The basic features are:
Changing enemies spawn logic. Now they will spawn exactly in that location where you are.
Decreasing enemies spawn delay. Now you don’t have to waste time waiting them to respawn :)
Changing enemies behaviour logic.
Changing spawn tables. This means the game can spawn stronger enemies instead of weak ones. Heavy SWATs instead of cops for instance.
Changing weapons used by enemies.

You can rewrite the script elements of each map (for example, energy and water elements is rewritten on the "counterfit" map. Part of the gameplay has been rewritten. Thus, on the counterfeit map, the logic of electric boxes and reels has been changed.

SETUP and EDIT:
if you want to play with this, you need to setup DAHM platform. After you need to copy the warmod folder to the "mods" folder.
How edit mod settings? - in warmod folder, open "configs" folder. And you can open 4 cfg:
eventlist.lua - event config( activate vault bulldozers on all diff, activate energy on countefeit and etc.. )
spawnlist.lua - change spawn enemy table( gensec on cloaker, shield, sniper )
weaponlist.lua - change weapons enemy( add bulldozer ak )
warmodcfg.lua - there you can activate/disable all mod functions.
WarmodCFG.EnableUniqueCopLogic - The police are much more dangerous now

!You should open cfg with "Notepad++" program, and edit cfg with encoding "utf-8" without BOOM.
But, i think, standart notepad you can use too ( It was noticed that due to the inappropriate encoding, the scripts were not readable by the game, That is why I advise you to use Notepad++ and edit the config with utf-8 encoding without BOOM ).

The mod complicates the gameplay precisely thanks to the introduced navigation (The police always know where the player is, and no one will be able to sit out, they will come for everyone. The situation becomes more complicated if the spawn graph is modified on the map.  It is not working on all maps, but it feels very good on first world bank. 

---------
Some things were not unfinished due to disagreements.
I posted the source code because it was available to some people. and they started using the modules for their own purposes. If you see that something like this is written in such a style, it was exclusively used for this mod.
Use wisely and make the game harder.
Good luck!

mod.name: DAHM/DorHUD Framework + mod collection
mod.desc:
NOTE: Due to many requests I decided to post this here. Since I'd rather have everything in one place and there's too much info for a comments section, I made a Steam group for the mod.

The mod, called DAHM (formerly known as DorHUD, but use whatever you like), is basically a collection of modifications to (in my eyes) improve the game. The core is comparable to BLT, but has a bunch of extra features and is now (almost) fully compatible with BLT since version 1.6. The mod is a framework that provides a way to add sub-modules, so that the whole thing is very customizable. The basic version comes bundled with a bunch of default submods to provide the most requested features without being intrusive or gameplay altering (for the most part).

The game is no longer officially supported and I therefore I assume that the executable will not be updated. If this is the case, then the mod has to be updated. But for now it fixes a few bugs, some well known and other not so much. I tried to patch the game crashing bugs, but I'm pretty sure I didn't get them all. A more known bug is that the Vyse masks (and others) disappear from time to time. This is because the Steam community group page is fetched and then checked for the presence of your Steam ID. This is not very reliable, so I replaced it with a call to your local Steam client to the groups you're in. Another thing is that the mute state is now preserved between games, so you don't have to mute people on every single map. And you can open the menu when someone is loading, etc., etc., etc. Just don't expect all solutions to be very elegant ;).

The majority of the sub-modules involve anticheat stuff and profile checking, simply because there are so many cheaters in this game that think they can do that without any consequences. Those that still want to ruin my games can only do it once with that account before they (manually) get added to a banlist. For now the list is only local, so nothing is shared (unless you count the manual sharing of it). Furthermore, there is a very simplistic HUD addon to keep track of the game time and the kills you've made, there's a new difficulty, you can add your own matchmaking filters and there's the possibility to ban players both by keeping a local file and by blocking them on Steam (the latter requires the provided hook).

Since I don't want to type things twice, more specific information can be found on the Steam group page. That's also where I try to provide support and where updates will be posted, so that everything is kept in one place.

mod.name: DAHM/DorHUD Framework + mod collection
mod.desc:
NOTE: Due to many requests I decided to post this here. Since I'd rather have everything in one place and there's too much info for a comments section, I made a Steam group for the mod.

The mod, called DAHM (formerly known as DorHUD, but use whatever you like), is basically a collection of modifications to (in my eyes) improve the game. The core is comparable to BLT, but has a bunch of extra features and is now (almost) fully compatible with BLT since version 1.6. The mod is a framework that provides a way to add sub-modules, so that the whole thing is very customizable. The basic version comes bundled with a bunch of default submods to provide the most requested features without being intrusive or gameplay altering (for the most part).

The game is no longer officially supported and I therefore I assume that the executable will not be updated. If this is the case, then the mod has to be updated. But for now it fixes a few bugs, some well known and other not so much. I tried to patch the game crashing bugs, but I'm pretty sure I didn't get them all. A more known bug is that the Vyse masks (and others) disappear from time to time. This is because the Steam community group page is fetched and then checked for the presence of your Steam ID. This is not very reliable, so I replaced it with a call to your local Steam client to the groups you're in. Another thing is that the mute state is now preserved between games, so you don't have to mute people on every single map. And you can open the menu when someone is loading, etc., etc., etc. Just don't expect all solutions to be very elegant ;).

The majority of the sub-modules involve anticheat stuff and profile checking, simply because there are so many cheaters in this game that think they can do that without any consequences. Those that still want to ruin my games can only do it once with that account before they (manually) get added to a banlist. For now the list is only local, so nothing is shared (unless you count the manual sharing of it). Furthermore, there is a very simplistic HUD addon to keep track of the game time and the kills you've made, there's a new difficulty, you can add your own matchmaking filters and there's the possibility to ban players both by keeping a local file and by blocking them on Steam (the latter requires the provided hook).

Since I don't want to type things twice, more specific information can be found on the Steam group page. That's also where I try to provide support and where updates will be posted, so that everything is kept in one place.

*Not all mods are posted to this website. Some smaller mods are posted in the [DAHM Downloads forum](https://steamcommunity.com/groups/dahm4pd/discussions/3/).*
